text.p: Italian bond futures were firmer but off the day's best levels after two reports from the European Commission and International Monetary Fund which suggested Italy may struggle to join Europe's single currency.
Dealers said that the market took heart from the Commission's view that Italy's deficit/GDP ratio this year could be 3.0 percent with effective and new budgetary measures.

The Commission's forecast the ratio at 3.2 percent for 1997 and 3.9 percent in 1998 before the effects of the 1998 budget, but the 3.2 percent figure, outside the three percent target, had been reported last week in an Italian newspaper.

The Commission report said that only Italy and Greece were set to miss the three percent goal, but the IMF report said Germany, France and Italy may miss the 1997 target. The IMF forecast the 1997 ratio at 3.3 percent.

Dealers said that the market took the figures largely in their stride, alarmed by the 3.9 percent 1998 figure but encouraged by the Commission's view that Italy could still make the three percent 1997 target with further measures.
"The figures were largely discounted by the market, as Italy could still make it if the political will is strong enough," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said the market was still underpined by encouraging preliminary data released by 11 sample cities on Monday and Tuesday which pointed to April CPI inflation falling to a 28-year low of 1.7 percent year-on-year, boosting hopes of a swift cut in the Bank of Italy's 6.75 percent discount rate.
